Red flags: 2022 protest against the Mac's drag storytime event
- On 31 July 2022 former TUV councillor Jolene Bunting and a handful of others protested outside the Mac against Dragtime Stories with Cherrie Ontop, a family story time event that was part of Belfast's Pride Weekend, because it was hosted by a drag queen (The Irish News, 1 August 2022).
- A counter-protest of up to two dozen people supported the event and outnumbered the protesters (The Irish News, 1 August 2022).
- The Mac's statement said its management "believe every child should enjoy creative experiences that fuel their imagination" and "We are proud to present Dragtime Stories for MAC families." (The Irish News, 1 August 2022).

SOURCES
- https://www.irishnews.com/news/northernirelandnews/2022/08/01/news/criticism_levelled_at_former_tuv_councillor_over_protest_at_drag_storytime_event_at_the_mac-2786722/
reason: The Irish News (1 August 2022) confirms the protest outside the Mac against an event the Mac itself presented ('We are proud to present Dragtime Stories for MAC families'), so it is aimed at the space's own programme, not at a hirer. Quotations word for word; one source, a named outlet.

CRITICISM IN ART MEDIA
1. Afterall: Eddie Chambers, "Iniva: Everything Crash" (2015)
URL: https://afterall.org/articles/iniva-everything-crash
- Chambers argues that although Iniva grew out of Black artists' activity and activism, it "only ever declared its embrace of Black artists in the most furtive of ways."
- He writes that the Arts Council was thinking in terms that amounted to "separate development for Black artists", and that Iniva became fixated on becoming a contemporary art gallery modelled on existing public institutions.
- He describes the Iniva of 2015 as practising "a dull top-down approach to its projects, with little to nothing in the way of lateral working relationships and collaborations."
- He concludes: "It perhaps goes without saying that it has failed those for whom it was, in part at least, established."

SOURCES
- https://afterall.org/articles/iniva-everything-crash
reason: Afterall essay by Eddie Chambers (2 July 2015) opened; all four quotations word for word. It criticises Iniva's own conduct (top-down programming, 'it has failed those for whom it was ... established'), not an exhibition, so it stays.
